# 2 Samuel Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 185r–186r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_015_page_001.jpg, 2SA_015_page_002.jpg, 2SA_015_page_003.jpg

---

**15:1** And-it-was from-after thus, and-made for-himself Avshalom a-chariot [merkavah] and-horses, and-fifty men running [ratsim] before-him.

**15:2** And-rose-early Avshalom and-stood upon [the]-side of-[the]-road of-the-gate. And-it-was, every man who had a-dispute [riv] to-come to the-king for-judgment [mishpat], and-called Avshalom to-him and-said, "From-what city [are]-you?" And-he-said, "From-one of-[the]-tribes of-Yisra'el [is]-your-servant."

**15:3** And-said to-him Avshalom, "See, your-words [are]-good and-right [tovim ve-nechochim], but-a-hearer [shome'a] there-is-not to-you from the-king."

**15:4** And-said Avshalom, "Who will-appoint-me [yesimeini] judge [shofet] in-the-land, and-upon-me every man who has a-dispute and-judgment [riv u-mishpat] would-come, and-I-would-do-him-justice [vehitsdaq'tihu]!"

**15:5** And-it-was when-drew-near a-man to-bow-down to-him, and-he-stretched-out his-hand and-seized him and-kissed him.

**15:6** And-did Avshalom according-to-this thing to-all Yisra'el who came for-judgment to the-king. And-stole [vayegannev] Avshalom [the]-heart [lev] of-[the]-men of-Yisra'el.

**15:7** And-it-was at-[the]-end of-forty years, and-said Avshalom to the-king, "Let-me-go, please, and-I-will-pay my-vow that I-vowed to-YHWH in-Chevron.

**15:8** For a-vow vowed your-servant when-I-dwelt in-Geshur in-Aram, saying, 'If returning YHWH-returns-me [yeshiveni] to-Yerushalayim, then-I-will-serve YHWH.'"

**15:9** And-said to-him the-king, "Go in-peace [lekh be-shalom]." And-he-rose and-went to-Chevron.

**15:10** And-sent Avshalom spies [meragelim] in-all [the]-tribes of-Yisra'el, saying, "When-you-hear [the]-sound of-the-shofar, then-you-shall-say, 'Reigned Avshalom in-Chevron!'"

**15:11** And-with Avshalom went two-hundred men from-Yerushalayim, called-ones [qeru'im], and-going in-their-innocence [betummam], and-not they-knew any thing.

**15:12** And-sent Avshalom [for] Achitofel the-Giloni, counselor [yo'ets] of-David, from-his-city, from-Gilo, while-he-sacrificed the-sacrifices. And-was the-conspiracy [qesher] strong ['amits], and-the-people going and-increasing with Avshalom.

**15:13** And-came the-one-reporting [ha-maggid] to David, saying, "Was [the]-heart of-[the]-men of-Yisra'el after Avshalom."

**15:14** And-said David to-all his-servants who [were] with-him in-Yerushalayim, "Arise, and-let-us-flee, for there-is-not to-us escape [peletah] from-[the]-face of-Avshalom. Hasten to-go, lest he-hasten and-overtake-us and-drive-upon-us the-evil [ra'ah] and-strike the-city [with]-[the]-edge of-[the]-sword."

**15:15** And-said [the]-servants of-the-king to the-king, "According-to-all that chooses my-lord the-king, behold, your-servants [are ready]."

**15:16** And-went-out the-king and-all his-house on-his-feet [beraglaw]. And-left the-king ten women, concubines [pilagshim], to-keep the-house.

**15:17** And-went-out the-king and-all the-people on-his-feet, and-stood at-Beth-ha-Merchaq [the-house of-the-distance].

**15:18** And-all his-servants [were]-passing over-him [al-yado], and-all the-Kereti and-all the-Peleti, and-all the-Gittim, six-hundred men who came on-his-feet from-Gat, [were]-passing upon [the]-face of-the-king.

**15:19** And-said the-king to Ittai the-Gitti, "Why do-you-go — also you — with-us? Return and-dwell with the-king, for a-foreigner [nokhriy] [are]-you, and-also an-exile [goleh] you [are] from-your-place.

**15:20** Yesterday [was]-your-coming, and-today shall-I-make-you-wander [ani'akha] with-us to-go? And-I [am]-going where I [am]-going [holekh al asher ani holekh]. Return and-take-back your-brothers. Covenant-faithfulness [chesed] and-faithfulness [emet] [be]-with-you."

**15:21** And-answered Ittai the-Gitti and-said, "As-lives YHWH, and-as-lives my-lord the-king, for in-the-place where will-be my-lord the-king, whether for-death or-for-life, for there will-be your-servant."

**15:22** And-said David to Ittai, "Go and-pass-over." And-passed-over Ittai the-Gitti and-all his-men and-all the-little-ones [ha-taf] that [were]-with-him.

**15:23** And-all the-land [were]-weeping [with]-a-voice great, and-all the-people [were]-passing-over. And-the-king [was]-passing-over in-[the]-wadi of-Qidron, and-all the-people [were]-passing-over upon [the]-face of-[the]-road the-wilderness [ha-midbar].

**15:24** And-behold, also Tsadoq and-all the-Leviyim with-him, bearing [the]-ark of-[the]-covenant of-God. And-they-set-down [the]-ark of-God, and-went-up Evyatar, until finished all the-people to-pass-over from the-city.

**15:25** And-said the-king to Tsadoq, "Return [the]-ark of-God to-the-city. If I-find favor [chen] in-[the]-eyes of-YHWH, then-he-will-bring-me-back and-show-me it and-his-habitation [naveihu].

**15:26** And-if thus he-says, 'Not I-have-delighted [chafatsti] in-you' — behold-me [hinneni], let-him-do to-me as-that-which [is]-good in-his-eyes."

**15:27** And-said the-king to Tsadoq the-priest, "A-seer [ro'eh] [are]-you? Return to-the-city in-peace [be-shalom], and-Achimaats your-son and-Yehonatan son of-Evyatar — your-two sons — with-you.

**15:28** See, I [am]-waiting [mahmiy] in-[the]-plains of-the-wilderness until comes a-word from-you to-report to-me."

**15:29** And-returned Tsadoq and-Evyatar [the]-ark of-God to-Yerushalayim, and-they-dwelt there.

**15:30** And-David [was]-going-up [oleh] in-[the]-ascent of-the-Olives [ma'aleh ha-zetim], going-up and-weeping [uvocheh], and-his-head [was]-covered to-him, and-he [was]-going barefoot [yachef]. And-all the-people that [were]-with-him covered each his-head, and-went-up, going-up and-weeping.

**15:31** And-David was-told, saying, "Achitofel [is] among-the-conspirators [ba-qosherim] with Avshalom." And-said David, "Make-foolish [sakkel-na], please, [the]-counsel of-Achitofel, YHWH."

**15:32** And-it-was — David came to the-summit [ha-rosh] where he-would-bow-down to-God — and-behold, to-meet-him [was] Chushai the-Arki, and-his-robe [kutonto] [was]-torn and-earth [was] upon his-head.

**15:33** And-said to-him David, "If you-pass-over with-me, then-you-will-be upon-me a-burden [le-massa].

**15:34** But-if to-the-city you-return and-you-say to-Avshalom, 'Your-servant I-[am], O-the-king; servant of-your-father I-[was] from-then [me'az], and-now I-[am]-also-your-servant' — then-you-shall-frustrate [hefarta] for-me [the]-counsel of-Achitofel.

**15:35** And-[is]-it-not — there with-you Tsadoq and-Evyatar the-priests? And-it-shall-be, every word that you-hear from-[the]-house of-the-king, you-shall-report to-Tsadoq and-to-Evyatar the-priests.

**15:36** Behold, there with-them [are]-their-two sons: Achimaats to-Tsadoq and-Yehonatan to-Evyatar. And-you-shall-send by-their-hand to-me every word that you-hear."

**15:37** And-came Chushai, friend [re'eh] of-David, to-the-city, and-Avshalom was-about-to-come to-Yerushalayim.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — yesimeini shofet:** "Who will appoint me judge!" — Absalom's exclamation echoes the pre-monarchic period when judges led Israel. His appeal bypasses the institution of kingship and appeals directly to popular desire for accessible justice. The irony is thick: he undermines his father's royal authority by invoking a pre-royal model of governance.

**v.6 — vayegannev lev:** "And-he-stole the heart." The verb *ganav* (steal) with *lev* (heart) is a powerful idiom for deceptive persuasion. Absalom does not win hearts — he steals them. The narrator's choice of verb is a moral judgment embedded in the description.

**v.7 — arba'im shanah:** "Forty years" — widely regarded as a scribal error for "four years" (*arba' shanim*), since Absalom's return from exile was only a few years prior. The Syriac Peshitta, some LXX manuscripts, and Josephus all read "four." The Leningrad Codex clearly reads "forty."

**v.20 — chesed ve-emet:** David's parting words to Ittai invoke the covenant pair *chesed* (covenant-faithfulness) and *emet* (truth/faithfulness). This is the language of divine covenant blessing, spoken to a foreign mercenary — a remarkable theological statement about the reach of God's grace.

**v.23 — nachal Qidron:** The Kidron Valley lies between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives. David's crossing of this wadi — weeping, barefoot, head covered — prefigures later theological crossings. The king goes out through the same valley he will later return through (cf. 19:16ff).

**v.25-26 — David's submission:** These verses contain David's most profound expression of trust in divine sovereignty. The conditional structure — "if I find favor... but if he says 'I have no delight in you'" — places the outcome entirely in YHWH's hands. The word *hinneni* (behold me / here I am) echoes Abraham (Gen 22:1) and Samuel (1 Sam 3:4).

**v.30 — ma'aleh ha-zetim:** The ascent of the Mount of Olives. David goes up weeping, head covered, barefoot — each detail a sign of mourning and humiliation. The scene is one of the most visually powerful in the entire Deuteronomistic History.

**v.37 — re'eh:** Hushai is called David's *re'eh* — "friend" or "companion." This may be a formal court title (cf. "King's Friend" in 1 Kgs 4:5), not merely a personal relationship.

*— EMET*
